operations.description: The root sends the whole vector to every other live node.
The root splits the vector into one block per live node, in rank order, and sends each node its block.
Every live node computes its own block and the root collects the blocks, in rank order, into one vector.

latencyBasis: Measured on the root around the whole transfer: a fresh lookup of CollectiveEndpoint in the target node's RMI registry (including RMI's distributed garbage collection "dirty" call when this process holds no other live stub for that endpoint), then the method call with its arguments and reply over a real loopback socket. Experiment 1 shows the lookup and the call as separate figures; here they are one.
payloadSizeBasis: Java serialization size (java.io ObjectOutputStream, stream header included); not the RMI wire bytes; primitive parameters are sized as primitives, as RMI marshals them
algorithmNote: Each collective is linear: the root handles the other ranks one after another in rank order, and only the root sends or asks. Real MPI libraries use trees (for example a binomial broadcast) so the root does not make every transfer itself; that is not built here. The root's own part never crosses the network. A failed transfer is reported and the collective goes on with the next rank; once the deadline has passed, no new transfer starts.

coHosting.reason: All nodes run inside one backend process on one computer, so they are separate nodes sharing a machine, not separate machines. Every transfer on this page still goes from the root through the target node's own RMI registry and a stub over a real loopback socket, so the lookup, the marshalling and the latency are real and measured; only the network distance between the nodes is missing.
